item.title: Why becoming a 'gatekeeper' for US protectionism is not in Mexico's interest
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-13 00:27:00
US Mexico Illustration: Xia Qing/GT Washington has erected a wall of protectionism around the globe, and Mexico is eager to pass it more bricks, helping plug the "loopholes." But the higher this wall rises, the more likely it is to hem in Mexico itself, constraining not only its development prospects but also its independence in shaping trade policy. According to Reuters, Luis Rosendo Gutierrez, Mexico's deputy economy minister for foreign trade, said on Wednesday that the Mexican government had tightened traceability measures with industry to ensure that no steel from China or other countries is rerouted through its territory into the US by exploiting Mexico's trade preferences. Meanwhile, Mexico is urging Washington to ease tariffs on Mexican steel, aluminum and automobiles. Jiang Shixue, a distinguished professor at Hangzhou Normal University, told the Global Times that Mexico's move is rooted in its economic predicament created by strong dependence on the US. Facing US tariff pressure and uncertainty surrounding the US-Mexico-Canada Agreement review, Mexico hopes that aligning itself with Washington's restrictions on trade with China will win concessions from the US. Since 2025, Mexico has repeatedly followed the US to announce measures to impose tariffs on imports from China and other countries without free-trade agreements. It seems that Mexico is actively standing guard at the door on Washington's behalf. While other countries may justify trade barriers as necessary to protect their own industries, Mexico's restrictions appear to be protecting the interests of a "third party." In effect, Mexico risks turning itself into a gatekeeper for Washington's protectionism. This could end up as a potential "Faustian bargain." Mexico hopes to sacrifice part of its economic and trade cooperation with China in exchange for US concessions on tariffs and trade. But it may discover that what it surrenders far outweighs what it could gain. On the one hand, Washington is unlikely to abandon its trade pressure on Mexico. On the other, Mexico risks sacrificing long-term industrial cooperation, supply chain diversification and, ultimately, its economic sovereignty. According to Gutierrez, the country has already reduced steel and aluminum imports from countries including China, South Korea and India, by about 30 percent. Zhou Mi, a researcher at the Chinese Academy of International Trade and Economic Cooperation, pointed out that manufacturing is a pillar of Mexico's economy, and steel and aluminum are essential inputs for industries such as auto manufacturing and machinery. Cutting imports of these materials could further aggravate supply pressures on Mexican manufacturers, disrupting production and undermining supply chain stability. More importantly, if Mexico can readily change its trade policies under external pressure, other countries may begin to question the stability and predictability of its investment and trade environment, he added. Once policy predictability is undermined, the price Mexico pays could go far beyond the immediate costs of tariffs. Just one day before the report, Mexican President Claudia Sheinbaum stressed that respect for sovereignty and cooperation free from subordination "are non-negotiable" tenets of Mexico's relations with the US. True sovereignty should not be confined to political rhetoric. It should be reflected in a country's ability to independently choose its trading partners, allocate resources according to its development needs and formulate its own economic and trade policies. In an increasingly interconnected global economy, broader international partnerships give countries greater room to maneuver amid external uncertainties. Canada, also deeply integrated into the North American economic system, has not abandoned efforts to diversify its trading partners and is actively seeking to expand cooperation with China and other economies to get rid of its dependence on the US. America's trade wall is America's choice. Mexico has no reason to turn it into its own barrier to development. What Mexico truly needs is not to become another brick in Washington's protectionist wall, but to safeguard its economic sovereignty, preserve its ability to connect with global markets and participate in international industrial chains. Otherwise, in trying to please Washington, Mexico risks cutting off its nose to spite its face.

item.title: Does Taiwan really understand major signals from this commemorative event?: Global Times editorial
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-13 00:23:00
A view of the Taiwan Straits is seen from Xiamen port, in East China's Fujian Province. Photo: IC Chinese communists are the most steadfast supporters, loyal collaborators, and faithful successors to the revolutionary cause initiated by Sun Yat-sen. No matter how "Taiwan independence" separatist forces attempt to stir up trouble, historical legitimacy and the moral high ground will always remain firmly with those who steadfastly advance national reunification and national rejuvenation. On the morning of November 12, a gathering commemorating the 160th anniversary of Sun Yat-sen's birth was held at the Great Hall of the People in Beijing. In his speech at the gathering, Chinese President Xi Jinping called for carrying forward the legacy of Sun, one of the nation's revered revolutionary forefathers, to make joint efforts for national rejuvenation and turn into reality the great dream of all Chinese people since the advent of modern times. Resolving the Taiwan question and achieving the complete reunification of the motherland are hurdles that must be overcome in the process of the great rejuvenation of the Chinese nation. At this important historical juncture, this high-profile commemoration carries profound contemporary significance and clearly sends extremely important signals. Do all sectors of Taiwan society, especially the island's authorities, get it? For Taiwan, the first signal lies in the significance of commemorating Sun for national reunification. "The spirit of patriotism," "national complete reunification" and "national rejuvenation" stand as inviolable historical orthodoxy and the moral high ground. Sun is a revolutionary forefather revered across the Taiwan Straits. Throughout his life, he traveled far and wide, with "revitalize the Chinese nation" as his most resounding rallying cry, and national reunification as his deepest concern. With remarkable historical foresight, he stated categorically: "Unification is the hope of all Chinese nationals. If China can be unified, all Chinese will enjoy a happy life; if it cannot be unified, they will suffer." This observation profoundly reveals that national unification and the well-being of the entire nation are inextricably bound together. By contrast, the current Democratic Progressive Party (DPP) authorities have engaged in political manipulation through "de-Sinicization" for the sake of partisan interests. While paying lip service to "freedom" and "democracy," they have, in practice, abandoned their historical roots and betrayed their own heritage. This is not only an outright desecration of the shared historical memory of people across the Taiwan Straits, but also a complete betrayal and insult to Sun's lifelong patriotic commitment. Beijing's solemn commemoration of Sun is a major blow against "Taiwan independence" separatist forces and a powerful rebuttal of their distorted view of history, setting the historical record straight. The second signal is to further clarify the mainland's policy stance on peaceful reunification and opposition to separatism under the evolving circumstances across the Taiwan Straits. "Compatriots on both sides of the Taiwan Straits are all Chinese. We are one family bound by blood ties that run deeper than water. As long as family members talk things through calmly and consult each other when issues arise, there are no disputes or differences that cannot be resolved." The political differences between the two sides of the Taiwan Straits are a legacy of history. However, as long as both sides uphold the one-China principle and the 1992 Consensus and sit down for face-to-face communication, there is nothing that cannot be discussed when it comes to the interests, well-being and development opportunities of Taiwan compatriots. Compatriots on both sides of the Straits are one family. Why should they allow themselves to be swayed by the antagonism deliberately stirred up by "Taiwan independence" separatist forces? Why should they allow external forces to turn Taiwan into a pawn in geopolitical rivalry? All sectors in Taiwan should recognize, in particular, that the door to peaceful reunification remains wide open, channels for exchanges and consultations remain accessible, and the interests and sentiments of Taiwan compatriots are given full consideration. They must not allow the DPP authorities' political manipulation in pursuit of "independence" to block the path of cross-Straits communication, much less allow a handful of politicians to hold Taiwan society's future hostage. The dead-end path of "Taiwan independence" separatism has already been firmly blocked. If the DPP authorities persist in seeking "independence by relying on external forces or military means," dragging the residents of Taiwan onto their war chariot, they will inevitably face a harsh reckoning by history and the people. The third signal is that only by adopting a broader historical perspective and an open-minded outlook befitting our times can we see through the layers of confusion, grasp the profound meaning of the principle that "family members should talk things through calmly." In the speech, President Xi highlighted Sun's lifelong devotion to the country, called for emulating, inheriting and carrying forward his invaluable spirit, and called for vigorously promoting the common values of humanity and actively advancing the building of a community with a shared future for humanity. Once we break free from the information cocoons and ideological prejudices created by "Taiwan independence" forces and examine the issue from the broader perspective of the great rejuvenation of the Chinese nation and the profound changes unseen in a century unfolding across the world, the logic becomes unmistakably clear. If humanity as a whole should work together to build a community with a shared future, there is even less reason for compatriots on both sides of the Taiwan Straits, bound by blood ties, to be artificially divided. The grand vision outlined by Sun in Fundamentals of National Reconstruction has not only become reality, but has also grown far richer and more expansive than he originally envisioned. History and reality have repeatedly demonstrated that Chinese communists are the most steadfast supporters, loyal collaborators, and faithful successors to the revolutionary cause initiated by Sun. No matter how "Taiwan independence" separatist forces attempt to stir up trouble, historical legitimacy and the moral high ground will always remain firmly with those who steadfastly advance national reunification and national rejuvenation. We sincerely hope that Taiwan compatriots will recognize the prevailing historical trend, distinguish right from wrong, and join their mainland compatriots in taking concrete action to shoulder the historic responsibility of achieving national reunification and national rejuvenation. The best way to honor Sun is to make the complete reunification of the motherland a reality!

item.title: China approves first oral GLP-1 weight-loss drug
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-12 23:45:00
Photo: VCG China on Thursday approved Eli Lilly's orforglipron pills, marketed domestically under the brand name "Muyouda," for long-term weight management in adults, making it the country's first oral GLP-1 medication approved for weight loss, according to the National Medical Products Administration (NMPA) and the company's press release on Thursday. According to the NMPA, the Class 1 innovative drug, submitted by Eli Lilly Nederland B.V., is intended for use alongside dietary changes and increased physical activity. It is approved for adults with an initial body mass index (BMI) of 30 kg/m² or above, or those with a BMI of at least 27 but below 30 kg/m² who have at least one weight-related condition, such as hypertension, dyslipidemia, high blood sugar, obstructive sleep apnea or cardiovascular disease. Orforglipron is an orally available, glucagon-like peptide-1 (GLP-1) receptor agonist that is approved as a weight loss agent.It is a small molecule that binds to the GLP-1 receptor in the brain that regulates appetite and satiety. Engagement of the GLP-1 receptor results in a decrease in hunger and food intake leading to loss of excessive weight, according to National Library of Medicine website. China is among the first countries to approve the medication. Its indication for treating adults with type 2 diabetes is still under review by the NMPA, according to the company. The medication was approved by the US Food and Drug Administration (FDA) in April, 2026, under the brand name Foundayo for weight management, according to TIME magazine. Global Times

item.title: GT Voice: AI jitters in US raise stakes in China for S.Korea chip firms
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-12 23:43:00
Production of semiconductor chip File photo: VCG South Korea's semiconductor exports are booming, but a new cloud is gathering over the industry - and it comes from the US. In a report published on Thursday, the Financial Times, under the headline "AI jitters erupt after Democrats threaten data center build-out," warned that the construction boom could be brought to a standstill following the Democrats' victories in the US midterm elections. The political headwinds facing US data centers could spill over into South Korea's semiconductor industry, at least in part. In January, The Korea Herald cited analysts as saying that most memory products shipped by South Korean companies to the US, including high bandwidth memory (HBM) and server DRAM, are used in artificial intelligence (AI) servers and data centers. This leaves South Korean memory chipmakers exposed to any slowdown in US data center development, which could put some of the demand underpinning their exports at risk. The US is an important market for South Korean semiconductors, even if it is not the largest. In July, Chosun Biz cited data from the Bank of Korea showing that the US ranked fourth among destinations for South Korean semiconductor exports in 2025, with shipments worth $19.02 billion, up from $13.626 billion three years earlier. Its share of South Korea's total semiconductor exports also edged up, from 9.6 percent to 10.3 percent. The question now is whether political resistance to data center construction in the US could put the brakes on the growth of its semiconductor demand - or even cause it to stall or decline. For South Korean chipmakers, this is a development that warrants close attention, as well as a clear assessment of what it could mean for their export prospects. Whatever the eventual impact on US semiconductor demand, the AI jitters unleashed by the midterm elections may be enough to prompt South Korean chipmakers to think ahead. If they seek to diversify their markets against the risk of slower growth in US demand, China is likely to be high on their lists. The Chinese mainland remained the largest destination for South Korean semiconductor exports in 2025, taking shipments worth $74.46 billion, or 40.3 percent of the total. This comes as South Korea presses ahead with plans to expand its semiconductor capacity. The Yonhap News Agency reported in September that the country plans to double its semiconductor production capacity within five years. Yet with the outlook for US AI investment becoming less certain, South Korean chipmakers may have to look increasingly to non-US markets to sustain their export growth, further increasing the importance of the Chinese market. If South Korean chipmakers turn increasingly to China, they could intensify competition and put greater pressure on Chinese domestic memory producers. But the picture is more complicated. Memory chip prices remain high, with some segments poised for further increases, pointing to the strength of underlying demand and the potential of the Chinese market. One factor that South Korean chipmakers should not underestimate is the rapid technological progress of China's memory producers. Once they overcome the remaining technical hurdles, China's extensive industrial supply chains and manufacturing capacity could allow them to scale up production quickly, turning technological advances into a formidable competitive advantage. For South Korean chipmakers to maintain or expand their presence in China, they will need to offer Chinese customers their most advanced products. Finding a way to overcome US restrictions that prevent advanced HBM exports to China is therefore essential to that effort. That task may become harder. The controversy surrounding Jensen Huang, who has resigned as Nvidia's CEO, has fueled fresh calls in Washington for tighter restrictions on China's access to advanced chips. But with semiconductors so vital to South Korea's economy, its chipmakers have every reason to press for greater room to sell their most advanced products in China. It is a market where competition is intensifying, but whose importance to South Korean suppliers is also growing. South Korea should assert its own economic interests.

item.title: Xi calls for carrying forward Sun Yat-sen's legacy in national rejuvenation drive
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-12 22:48:00
A gathering to commemorate the 160th anniversary of Sun Yat-sen's birth is held in Beijing, capital of China on November 12, 2026. Photo: Xinhua Chinese President Xi Jinping on Thursday called for carrying forward the legacy of Sun Yat-sen, one of the nation's revered revolutionary forefathers, to make joint efforts for national rejuvenation and turn into reality the great dream of all Chinese people since the advent of modern times. Xi, also general secretary of the Communist Party of China (CPC) Central Committee and chairman of the Central Military Commission, made the remarks at a gathering held in Beijing to commemorate the 160th anniversary of Sun's birth, the Xinhua News Agency reported Thursday. Born in 1866, Sun led the Revolution of 1911 more than a century ago to abolish the absolute monarchy that had ruled China for thousands of years. He died in 1925. Thursday marks the 160th anniversary of Sun Yat-sen's birth. Xi noted that Chinese communists are the most steadfast supporters, loyal collaborators, and faithful successors to the revolutionary cause initiated by Sun. For more than 100 years, the CPC has led the Chinese people in writing the most magnificent chapter in the history of the Chinese nation, Xi said, calling on the Chinese people to carry forward Sun's unyielding determination, rise to challenges ahead and break new ground in the country's development. Call for unity Calling on people to learn from Sun's commitment to unity, Xi also emphasized adhering to the united front and strengthening the great unity among all the sons and daughters of the Chinese nation. Resolving the Taiwan question and realizing the complete reunification of the motherland is an unwavering historical mission for the CPC, the shared aspiration of all Chinese people, and a natural requirement for the great rejuvenation of the Chinese nation, Xi stressed. People on both sides of the Taiwan Straits and all Chinese at home and abroad should join hands to oppose the "Taiwan independence" secessionist forces, and work together for the peaceful development of cross-Straits relations and the complete reunification of the motherland, Xi said. Zheng Jian, a professor at the Taiwan Research Institute of Xiamen University, said Sun's legacy carries particular relevance nowadays amid growing international tensions, stressing that people on both sides of the Taiwan Straits have every reason to unite in pursuing national rejuvenation rather than allowing internal divisions or external interference to undermine their shared interests. A peaceful resolution of the Taiwan question under the "one country, two systems" framework could offer a model for addressing similarly complex historical and political disputes elsewhere in the world, Zheng told the Global Times. Visitors pay tribute at Sun Yat-sen Memorial Hall on 160th anniversary of his birth. Photo: Li Hao/Global Times Wide celebration Beijing is hosting a series of exhibitions and cultural events throughout November to commemorate the Restoration of Taiwan and the 160th anniversary of Sun's birth, drawing more than 1,200 participants from both sides of the Taiwan Straits, including nearly 100 who traveled from Taiwan, Zhang Han, spokesperson for the State Council Taiwan Affairs Office, said on Wednesday. On Thursday, visitors gathered at the Sun Yat-sen Memorial Hall in Beijing's Xiangshan. They paused before displays of Sun's handwritten manuscripts, writings and personal artifacts, reflecting on the legacy of a man whose lifelong ambition was to revive a nation weakened by decades of turmoil and foreign aggression, the Global Times reporter observed. A visitor surnamed Zheng told the Global Times that he had made a special trip to the memorial hall to mark Sun's birthday, drawn by the story of a revolutionary who helped bring down China's centuries-old imperial system at a time when the country was struggling against foreign aggression and internal turmoil. "His story inspires me to keep fighting for what I believe in, no matter how difficult the circumstances," he said. "I will always remember his words: 'The revolution has not yet succeeded; comrades, you must strive on.'" Chi Chia-lin, honorary chairman of the Reunification Alliance Party in Taiwan and a Taiwan-based historian, traveled to Beijing to participate in the anniversary activities. Chi told the Global Times that despite Taiwan authority's absurd "de-Sinicization" effort, Sun is still widely and highly respected and his legacy is remembered by people in Taiwan. "Both sides of the Taiwan Straits share a common understanding and appreciation of Sun Yat-sen's historical legacy, making joint commemorations of the revolutionary leader a particularly meaningful and constructive undertaking amid current cross-Straits tensions," Chi said. Visitors pay tribute at Sun Yat-sen Memorial Hall on 160th anniversary of his birth. Photo: Li Hao/Global Times Guangzhou, the southern China city where Sun helped lay the groundwork for the revolution, will host a five-day exchange program from November 12 to 16, bringing together scholars, political commentators and young media professionals from both sides of the Taiwan Straits. A six-episode documentary titled "Sun Yat-sen" has aired simultaneously since November 8 to commemorate Sun's anniversary. In Hong Kong, the anniversary has been marked with an official commemorative ceremony and the release of a special stamp collection highlighting Sun's historical ties to the city, where he studied, organized revolutionary activities and delivered public speeches, Hong Kong media reported. DPP's fruitless thwart However, the anniversary of Sun's birth appears to have struck a nerve with Taiwan's Democratic Progressive Party (DPP), which, fearing that Sun's legacy could reinforce a shared sense of Chinese identity among people on both sides of the Taiwan Straits, has sought to discourage Taiwan residents from participating in commemorative events. Taiwan's so-called "Mainland Affairs Council (MAC)" recently said that applications from people on the island who require official permission to travel to the mainland to attend the events related to Sun's birth anniversary would not be approved. It also urged people from other sectors not to travel to the mainland, Hong Kong, or Macao special administrative regions to participate in or co-organize related activities. Over the years, the DPP authorities have faced repeated accusations of seeking to erase Sun's legacy. During Lai Ching-te's tenure as mayor of Tainan, a controversy over the removal of a statue of Sun prompted protesters to camp out for days in opposition. Pro-DPP figures have proposed removing requirements to display Sun's portrait, while pro-independence groups have called for Yat-sen street named after him to be renamed. Earlier this year, the DPP authorities pushed for a redesign of Taiwan's banknotes, raising concerns that Sun's portrait could be removed from the currency, according to a People's Daily report. Sun Yali, president of the Sun Yat-sen Culture Foundation in Zhongshan and representative of Sun Yat-sen's family, told the China News Service on Wednesday that she is concerned many young people on the island of Taiwan have become so unfamiliar with Sun Yat-sen that some cannot even identify him when they encounter his statue. The fading historical memory has left her saddened, frustrated and, at times, angry. The DPP is particularly wary, as it fears commemorations of Sun Yat-sen, a revolutionary figure revered on both sides of the Taiwan Straits, would evoke identification with the shared history and cultural heritage. But no matter what tricks the DPP authorities play, they cannot alter the fact that both sides of the Taiwan Straits belong to one China, sever the deep historical and cultural bonds between people across the Straits, erase the imprint of Chinese culture on Taiwan society, or reverse the inevitable trend toward national reunification, Zheng said.

item.title: World eyes on key topics, potential trilateral talks at APEC meeting after China-US FM call
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-12 22:29:00
China US Photo: VCG With the clock ticking down toward the 2026 APEC Economic Leaders' Meeting, a call between the Chinese and US foreign ministers dominated media coverage on Thursday, which zeroed in on the priorities each side emphasized and whether a potential China-Russia-US trilateral meeting would take place on the sidelines of next week's meeting. Chinese analysts said these differing priorities reflect the fact that while both sides seek to stabilize relations, they still have different considerations on specific issues, and how to address each other's concerns on equal terms is a question to be resolved in the future. Washington is seeking to use this year's APEC meeting to advance its own priority agenda, and appears to believe that, if this trilateral meeting materializes, it would be an opportunity to showcase diplomatic gains, they added. Reciprocity the next test Chinese Foreign Minister Wang Yi on Wednesday held phone talks with US Secretary of State Marco Rubio. The two sides had an in-depth exchange of views on China-US relations and the interaction between the two heads of state, Xinhua reported. During the talks, Wang, also a member of the Political Bureau of the Communist Party of China Central Committee, said that the two heads of state agreed to enrich the connotation of a new vision of China-US relations, providing clearer strategic guidance for exploring a correct approach for the two countries to get along with each other. China's Foreign Ministry described the phone talks as "positive and constructive" in a statement published on Wednesday. The US State Department readout also noted that the two recalled the leaders' "commitment to a constructive relationship of strategic stability on the basis of respect, fairness, and reciprocity." Yang Xiyu, a senior research fellow at the China Institute of International Studies, told the Global Times on Thursday that this call sends a positive political signal. It reflected a shared desire on both sides to build on the progress achieved at the previous leaders' meeting and to keep advancing China-US relations. Following the building of a constructive China-US relationship of strategic stability, the call demonstrated a common willingness to inject more substantive content into that relationship through concrete cooperation and effective management of differences, and to ensure that it truly takes root and delivers tangible results, Yang added. While China and the US share an intent to yield practical results under the framework of a constructive China-US relationship of strategic stability, their priorities over its specific components diverge. The stable momentum of China-US relations has not come easily and is the two major countries' rational choice based on their respective and common interests, Wang said, according to the Chinese Foreign Ministry's statement. China, having maintained a stable and consistent policy toward the US, is willing to strengthen communication and cooperation with the US side, properly handle differences and sensitive issues, support each other in hosting the 2026 APEC Economic Leaders' Meeting and the G20 Summit, and work to bring a constructive China-US relationship of strategic stability into effect and deliver results, Wang said. Yang said China's core concern is the Taiwan question, and it demands that the US honor its commitments and strictly abide by the three China-US joint communiques. In the economic and trade sphere, China is likewise concerned about US trade-restrictive measures and supply chain stability, he added. Wang's emphasis this time on properly handling differences and sensitive issues can also be understood as an early diplomatic signal aimed at prompting the US to take potential risks seriously and to strengthen communication and management before problems arise, Zhang Jiadong, a professor at the Center for American Studies, Fudan University, told the Global Times. The US readout said that "they agreed on the importance of meaningful leader-level conversations to advance goals such as peace and denuclearization, including at any potential trilateral leaders meeting with Russia." Reuters reported that "China's earlier readout of the call between [US Secretary of State Marco] Rubio and Wang made no mention of talks on denuclearization or a trilateral summit with Russia." Zhang said that the divergent priorities laid out by China and the US stem from their respective roles and diplomatic objectives at the APEC meeting in Shenzhen. As the host, China's key priority is to create conditions for productive exchanges among leaders and advance global peace and stability, he said, adding that the US, by contrast, seeks to leverage this diplomatic gathering to push forward its own priority agendas. Within a constructive China-US relationship of strategic stability, the two countries should build up results by proceeding incrementally, said Yang, stressing that China has maintained consistency and continuity in its policy toward the US, which also creates conditions for the two sides to identify areas of cooperation. Trilateral meeting in focus Apart from the bilateral ties between Beijing and Washington, some foreign media are closely watching the prospect of a trilateral encounter involving China, Russia and the US at next week's APEC gathering. From November 1 to November 12, Chinese Foreign Ministry spokespersons have taken five related questions, with consistent responses: "China is in communication with relevant parties regarding a meeting between the three heads of state." The US readout said that they agreed on "any potential trilateral leaders meeting with Russia." In a Thursday report, Bloomberg led its headline with the prospect of the trilateral talks, noting that the US-China call "adds momentum" to a potential summit with Russia. Zhang said Washington's push for the potential China-Russia-US leaders' meeting partly stems from its desire to notch up diplomatic wins on the global stage and project its diplomatic clout. A trilateral meeting would carry substantial political symbolism, especially amid the current international landscape and the backdrop of US domestic politics. Both Russian and US leaders may seek to project diplomatic influence through such an encounter, according to Zhang. The US may also hope the potential gathering can reinstate relevant dialogue mechanisms and put guardrails around risks tied to US-Russia relations and the Ukraine conflict, preventing the situation from spiraling out of control, said Yang. Should trilateral talks take place down the line, they must be guided by the principle of addressing each side's concerns on a reciprocal basis, Chinese experts noted.

item.title: Tokens join China's Double 11 for first time as real-world AI applications drive demand for computing power
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-12 20:07:00
Concept picture of Token Photo: VCG Tokens, the units used to meter and bill large-language model usage, became a new promotional category on Chinese e-commerce platforms for the first time during this year's Double 11 shopping festival, with Zhipu, MiniMax, and DeepSeek offering discounts of up to 50 percent on selected products on e-commerce platforms such as Alibaba-backed Taobao. The sale also attracted many shoppers. Wang Ning, a 30-year-old worker in Beijing, spent 200 yuan (about $30) buying tokens on Taobao recently. He told the Global Times on Thursday that for him, the bigger shift is not just cheaper access, but what the shopping cart now stands for. "A few years ago, Double 11 meant stocking up on household goods. Now I'm stocking up on computing power the same way. That tells you how fast artificial intelligence has moved from a developer tool to something ordinary consumers just buy like a phone plan." Businesses are also reading the moment as a structural turn. Li Fanyiran, a data scientist working at Bilibili, told the Global Times on Thursday that his team began using large-language AI models for data labeling in 2023, and it has since folded AI agents into customer service, advertising placement and diagnostic analysis. "Seeing tokens on a Double 11 shelf is a signal the industry has crossed a line, and computing services are no longer just infrastructure sitting behind the scenes. They're now packaged, priced and sold like any other consumer product. That changes how companies think about AI: not as research and development, but as a measurable, buyable input." A Tmall representative said that sales in the platform's Token category rose 450 percent on October 20, the first day of its Double 11 sales campaign, compared to the previous day. Buyers mainly included individuals and small and medium-sized businesses with specific AI needs, such as households, users engaged in learning and research, and "one-person companies," the Economic Information Daily reported. The use of AI services in China has also continued to grow. According to the Large Model Token Service Performance Monitoring Report (2026), released by the China Academy of Information and Communications Technology earlier this month, China's average daily token consumption reached approximately 500 trillion in June 2026, nearly four times the level recorded in December 2025. Liu Dingding, a technology industry analyst, told the Global Times on Thursday that the move reflects a deeper reset in both retail and tech. "Double 11 used to reflect China's consumption power in physical goods. Putting tokens on the same shelf shows the center of gravity is moving, from selling things to selling intelligence. For the tech industry, it means the competition is no longer just who builds the better model, but who can turn that model into a service millions of ordinary people are willing to pay for." Taking the short-drama industry as an example, Liu said that AI-generated content can reduce some of the costs associated with locations, filming and personnel. For producers able to publish AI-generated content on online platforms and generate commercial returns, spending on tokens has become part of their production costs. Demand for paid computing power services is likely to grow as AI applications expand, he added. AI services also made their way into livestream shopping sessions hosted by major online influencers. On November 2, Chinese e-commerce livestream host Li Jiaqi launched a token promotion on Taobao. According to information released by Qianwen Office, nearly 100,000 monthly personal membership plans were sold within half an hour of the launch, representing a combined allowance of approximately 2 trillion tokens. Previously, token services were mainly purchased through AI model providers' official websites and developer platforms. On September 3, Tmall launched its token recharge center, initially connecting providers including Alibaba Cloud, Zhipu, Kimi and MiniMax, and offering both subscription-based and pay-as-you-go services. JD.com also introduced an AI software recharge section, adding large-language packages and AI application memberships to its online marketplace.

item.title: New evidence of the Japanese troops' biological and chemical warfare crimes in China unveiled
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-12 17:01:00
An exhibit depicting gas masks and other equipment used by Unit 731 at the 9.18 History Museum in Shenyang, Northeast China's Liaoning Province Photo: VCG Marking the 80th anniversary of the opening of the International Military Tribunal for the Far East, or the Tokyo Trials this year, dozens of Chinese experts and scholars unveiled new evidence, discoveries and research findings on the Japanese military's biological and chemical warfare crimes in China, Xinhua News Agency reported on Thursday. Jin Shicheng, a curator at the Exhibition Hall of Evidences of Crime Committed by Unit 731 of the Japanese Imperial Army, unveiled new findings from Unit 731 and Unit 516 archival records, revealing how Unit 516's "residual affairs cleanup unit" was tasked with handling matters in the aftermath of Japan's defeat. According to Jin, the roughly 70-member unit was responsible for transporting, burying and abandoning chemical weapons before the main Japanese forces retreated. Records about the unit's members may offer clues to the burial sites of chemical weapons left behind by the Japanese military, potentially offering a breakthrough in locating the weapons. As the first post-World War II tribunal specifically established to try Japan's biological warfare crimes, the Khabarovsk Trial filled a gap left by the Tokyo Trials, which failed to bring the members of Unit 731 to justice for their atrocities. Gong Wenjing, director of the international research center on Unit 731 at the Harbin Academy of Social Sciences, said that cross-referencing archives from China, the US, Japan and Russia has strengthened the body of evidence documenting the Japanese troops' biological warfare operations. Declassified Russian archives on the Khabarovsk Trial, historical materials handed over by Russia to China, together with declassified US documents and Japanese historical records, are gradually helping piece together the full picture of the Soviet Union's trial of Japanese war criminals responsible for biological warfare. Modern biotechnology is unlocking evidence from physical remains. Soil tests by Chinese researchers have provided biological evidence that Unit 731 conducted anthrax weaponization research in the area around the Sifang Building area of its former headquarters. Wang Meng, a history professor at Wuhan University, outlined two key research findings. Victims' remains unearthed at the former Japanese army medical school site in Tokyo bore widespread signs of cutting, drilling and brain surgery, demonstrating the Japanese military's cruel human experiments. Cholera toxin genes detected in the skull remains of 41 victims unearthed at Jiuhua Mountain in Nanjing have provided further evidence of Japanese military human experiments in East China. As Japanese right-wing forces seek to downplay, distort and even deny the crimes of the Japanese Imperial Army's bacteriological and chemical warfare during its invasion of China, participating experts hold that in-depth exploration of archival materials is key to building a body of evidence and refuting historical nihilism. item.title: China's Mazu early weather warning box makes global debut
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-12 11:14:00
China intelligent meteorological solution MAZU is seen on display during the 2026 World Artificial Intelligence Conference in Shanghai. Photo: VCG China's Mazu all-in-one box, an intelligent meteorological early warning solution, was officially launched globally at the COP31 High-Level Forum on South-South Cooperation on Climate Change in Antalya, Turkey, the China Meteorological Administration (CMA) said in a WeChat post on Thursday. MAZU, short for multi-hazard, alert, zero-gap and universal, is an AI-driven meteorological early warning platform named after the Chinese guardian goddess of the sea. The box is a lightweight, integrated hardware-software early warning solution designed to run the Mazu platform locally. It integrates storage, intelligent computing, networking, display and computation. Compatible with Ethernet, 5G and satellite communications, it delivers capabilities including nowcasting, an overview dashboard, operational monitoring and on-site AI assistance, enabling developing countries to rapidly ingest local observational data, according to the release. The box can run operations independently on site or connect to cloud resources and integrate with existing operational systems for coordinated operations. It supports modular expansion and continuous upgrading, helping local agencies strengthen their early warning operational capabilities, said the release. Given wide climatic variations worldwide, the CMA has worked closely with national meteorological and hydrological agencies to adapt Mazu into a weather tool tuned to local conditions. On November 1, China officially delivered a Mazu all-in-one box to Sri Lanka, which is expected to enter operational service by the end of 2026. It features custom-built modules for aviation, maritime and other sectors, aiming to help the Southern Asian country shore up its multi-hazard meteorological early-warning capabilities, CMA said. China delivered a customized version of its homegrown AI-powered meteorological early warning system to Nepal on September 22 to help the country improve early warning and disaster response. The move came after the CMA gave Nepal's meteorological department a version of Mazu for cloud-based trial use on August 29, following a deadly mudslide at the Gyirong-Rasuwa border crossing on the China-Nepal border, the Xinhua News Agency reported. As of October 2026, the Mazu solution had been deployed in eight countries, including Pakistan, Ethiopia and Sri Lanka, and tested through cloud-based trials in more than 50 countries, according to CMA.
